title: Overlap producers and consumers only with an explicit streaming protocol

values: plan or work overlaps producers and consumers through incremental artifact delivery
facts.note: Governing fact: whether producers and consumers overlap via incremental artifacts is judged from plan/task content. Lexical terms alone never activate the rule.
Supporting signal only; used to route candidate tasks to the semantic finding above, not to activate the rule by itself.

fires: A plan proposes that a consumer wagon start processing chunks before the producer wagon finishes, to cut first-result latency.
A plan for a large chunked workload proposes streaming between producer and consumer to keep memory bounded.
A plan proposes streaming artifacts across interlocking boundaries.
doesNotFire: A plan uses a standard finish-to-start journey handoff with whole artifacts and proposes no overlap.
A task mentions 'pipeline' or 'chunk' (e.g. a CI pipeline) but does not overlap producers and consumers through incremental artifacts.

given: A journey with producers and consumers; pipelining is meant for streaming/chunked workloads where first-result latency or memory dominates
when: the planner overlaps producers and consumers through incremental artifact delivery
then: Overlap them only with an explicit streaming protocol that preserves backpressure, ordering, partial failure, stream completion and resource bounds.
prefer: Acceptances that test slow consumers, bounded buffers, chunk order, interruptions and equivalence, and that measure throughput and first-result latency.
avoid: Treating a standard journey handoff as if it defined streaming.
Planning cross-interlocking streaming without new declared runtime semantics (internal wagon streaming is possible).
Inferring unimplemented orchestration behavior from this pattern, or treating it as a new runtime dispatch option.
why: A standard journey handoff does not define streaming, so overlap is only sound when the protocol is explicit and its properties are preserved and tested.
evidence: Plan names an explicit streaming protocol, and acceptances show backpressure, ordering, partial failure, stream completion and resource bounds are preserved.
Acceptances test slow consumers, bounded buffers, chunk order, interruptions and equivalence; throughput and first-result latency are measured.
Any cross-interlocking streaming is backed by new declared runtime semantics.
Existing plan and source validators pass.
verifier_detail: Guidance for agents, not independent enforcement; existing plan and source validators apply.
audit: Graph: requires planner.journey.execution-strategies (shared applicability and evidence principles).

additions.text: overlap is only sound when the protocol is explicit and its properties are preserved and tested
additions.justification: Restates S006/S010/S011/S013 as the reason; adds no new obligation or claim beyond the source.

trace.note: Name kept in audit; title reflects statement.
Kept as applicability guidance, not as an exclusion.
